items.title: Consent first, not afterwards
items.body: Both sides agree the industry built first and consulted later, and was punished for it. The same applies on a small scale in a surgery. Bring patients and staff along before a scribe or triage tool goes live, explain what is recorded and why, and make opting out easy.

items.title: American rules still shape our suppliers
items.body: NLW expects modest US rules on pre-release testing, incident reporting and liability. They do not bind the NHS, but most of our vendors build on American models. Clearer liability for model builders would help when a scribe gets something wrong; until then the clinician who signs the note carries it.

items.title: Little direct clinical relevance, some price risk
items.body: This was an edition about US politics. The practical point is cost: if tougher local terms make data centres dearer, as NLW expects, or financing falters, as Zitron expects, AI service prices could move. Prefer shorter contracts with a clear exit and data export.
